{"answer":"Transformer-based recommenders can amplify popularity bias as they scale: greater depth may cause spectral collapse in predictions, leading to more recommendations of popular items and fewer of niche items. SPRINT mitigates this by regularizing attention scores and feed-forward parameters, improving accuracy and long-tail fairness in the reported experiments. [1]\n\nOther approaches include BT-SR, a Transformer-based sequential recommender that uses noncontrastive self-supervised learning to improve long-tail coverage and calibration [8], and PopSteer, which steers popularity-related neuron activations in a sequential recommendation model to improve fairness with minimal accuracy impact. [6]","grounded":true}"}
